title: Phased intake orchestration and remediation commitments for private/VPC on-prem requests
creator: Priya Raman
description: Problem: We get a steady stream of private/VPC/on-prem requests that rely on diverse networking constraints (eg restricted egress, behind corp proxies, intermittent NAT, strict egress windows). Current intake is ad-hoc, causing long lead times and repeated rework. Goal: build a phased intake orchestration that automates initial risk-banding, provides explicit remediation commitments (timeboxed), and creates a predictable customer promise for network-sensitive private deployments. This ticket scopes a product-managed playbook + lightweight automation for triage, plus a contract template for remediation SLAs and a self-serve technical readiness checklist for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Automated intake form captures minimal network posture signals (eg allowed IPs, egress restrictions, proxy type, acceptable maintenance windows)
Risk-banding logic implemented server-side and surfaced to PM/SE with suggested engagement lane (Self-serve / Concierge / Fast-track)
Three remediation commitment tiers defined (14d remediation, 45d remediation with concierge, 90d expansion runway) with templated customer comms
Self-serve edge-proxy template and ephemeral-egress instructions published (Confluence + Drive) and referenced from intake
Runbook for staged testing (smoke, perf, upgrade window) created and validated by Eng and Security
Dashboard card in Console prototype shows: open private-intake count, stage, estimated remediation SLA, and blocker reasons

tradeoffs: Speed vs accuracy of risk-banding: fast heuristic banding reduces triage latency but increases manual follow-ups; we mitigate by surfacing confidence score and forcing SE verification for low-confidence bands.
Service promise rigidity: firm remediation SLAs improve predictability for customers but increase contractual exposure; we propose guarded SLAs with 'pause on customer-blocker' clauses.
Automation surface area: deep automation requires more upfront engineering investment; prefer a phased approach (heuristic -> telemetry-backed rules -> ML) to keep scope contained.
Support load: introducing a self-serve lane reduces concierge demand long-term but requires better docs and onboarding flows to avoid ticket storms during launch.
